prompt: Paint an intimate evening theater box-office counter in opaque gouache. A small tangerine-orange paper admission ticket rests flat across the palm of a white cotton glove lying on the counter. Make the ticket the first thing the eye picks out even in miniature: a concentrated orange rectangle, precise punched paper edge and a fine contact shadow against a quiet blue-violet gray fold. In the glove keep a passage of pale neutral pearl cloth next to muted indigo-violet cast light in folds; soft seams and a hint of cotton weave give it its own white fabric color. Let the glove’s outer contour meet a softly violet-lit counter of similar value, with the booth window only suggested beyond. Matte opaque brush shapes, varied dry brush at the folds, restrained background edges.

Make a transparent watercolor of a teahouse window table at sunset. One small red raspberry sits on a pale celadon-glazed plate. Give the berry the first glance: clustered crimson drupelets and a compact dark contact wash against an open area of delicate cool celadon. Let diluted blue-green wash show the plate’s body color beside a small amber window reflection; show the glaze with a soft translucent sheen. Around the plate let the table pick up a wash of similar light value so its outside rim is quiet. Keep the far window and amber sunset soft, with transparent layered washes, a few blooms and reserved paper. Intimate still life, berry small in relation to the dish.

Draw a carpenter’s workbench under a blue work lamp entirely in colored pencil on fine-grained paper. One small yellow carpenter’s pencil with a flat rectangular shaft is tucked into the pocket of a black leather tool pouch; let the pocket lip visibly cross the lower part of the pencil. Give the exposed yellow shaft and its cut wooden tip the crispest edge and strongest local contrast, visible on first glance. Keep the grain and pliable folds of the leather black in the midtones, with a restrained cool blue glint on a fold. Behind the pouch use similarly dark bench wood near its outside edge, some subdued wood grain to place it in the workshop. Fine layered pencil strokes and paper tooth; the surroundings stay quiet.

Photograph a still life in a kitchen lit by blue dawn window light. One small green olive sits on a shallow copper tray. Frame from a gently elevated oblique viewpoint with the olive in critical focus. Let its distinctly green skin and one pinpoint reflection catch the eye immediately against a quiet copper plane with a soft contact shadow. Keep warm muted reddish copper visible in the tray body, a broad diffuse blue reflection revealing metal and the morning light. The surface around the perimeter is close in brightness to the tray; soften the rim reflection and let a hint of the kitchen recede in the background. Natural photographic exposure, subtle rolled rim, fine scratches, credible scale.

Draw a pre-performance dressing-room still life in soft pastel. One small silver dragonfly brooch is pinned to the side of a navy felt hat. Bring the eye first to its small clear four-winged silver shape against a quiet uninterrupted patch of deep navy felt; a few fine bright silver strokes define its wings and narrow body. Let the hat retain its intrinsic dark navy in its middle tones, with fine broken strokes for felt nap and a gentle pink cast on a turned plane. Bring the softly lit dressing-room background close in value to the hat around most of its outer silhouette. Soft chalk edges and rubbed pink ambient color suggest the mirror area in the distance; no bright competing lights. Keep the brooch physically small and attached flush to the crown.
